category_title: Students with mild disabilities exhibiting high rates of non-responsiveness and passive off-task behavior
scenario_title: Passive disengagement during unstructured time and paper-pen activities
minimal_context: The student is expected to complete a paper-pen math worksheet during general classroom instruction.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Alright everyone, I have handed out the math worksheet. Please take out your pencils and start working on the problems.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Looks around the classroom without taking out a pencil or looking at the worksheet.)

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: You need to get started on your assignment now.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Continues to sit quietly, engaging in self-stimulation by repeatedly tapping his fingers on the edge of the desk, without raising his hand or participating in the task.)

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Are you going to write down the answers?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Displays no academic response and no task management, spending the time doing nothing and staring blankly during the paper-pen activity.)

task.content: General classroom instruction across various content areas including math problems, paper-pen activities, and teacher lecture

context.social_setting: Whole group instruction, teacher lecture, and discussion

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: During teacher lecture and conditions such as no instruction, no task, no activity, and paper-pen activities
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: spend almost one fourth of the instruction time by doing nothing, displaying no academic response, no task management, and no competing response

behavior_patterns.condition: In no instruction, no activity and no task conditions
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: looking around which was coded in 20.10% of the intervals and self stimulation which was observed in 10.49 % of the observation time
displayed very few academic behaviors such as silent reading and academic talking in conjunction with task management behaviors, such as raising their hand and task participation
